drive.title: Your own Google client
drive.why: rclone's built-in Google client is shared by every rclone user, so Google throttles it (slow listings, "rate limit exceeded"), and it stops working during 2026. A client of your own is free, and any Google account can own it.

steps.title: Create a project
steps.text: Sign in to Google Cloud with any Google account and create a project. Any name works, for example CloudKit.

steps.title: Enable the Google Drive API
steps.text: With the new project selected at the top of the page, click Enable.

steps.title: Set up the consent screen
steps.text: Click Get started. App name: anything (rclone is fine). Support email: yours. Audience: External (Internal only reaches accounts of your own Workspace). Add your contact email, accept the terms and click Create.

steps.title: Add the Drive scopes
steps.text: Click Add or remove scopes, paste these into Manually add scopes, click Add to table and Update, then Save at the bottom of the page.

steps.title: Publish the app
steps.text: Click Publish app and confirm. Google's review is not needed for personal use. An app left in Testing works too, but its sign-in expires every 7 days; if you keep it there, add yourself under Test users.

steps.title: Create the client
steps.text: Application type: Desktop app, any name, then Create. Copy the client ID and the client secret it shows into the fields below.

drive.signin_note: Google warns that it hasn't verified the app. It is your own: choose Advanced, then Go to … (unsafe).

id.label: Client ID
id.error: A Google client ID ends in .apps.googleusercontent.com

secret.label: Client secret
secret.error: That doesn't look like a client secret

dropbox.title: Your own Dropbox app
dropbox.why: rclone's built-in Dropbox app key is shared by every rclone user. An app of your own gets limits of its own. It is free, and any Dropbox account can own it.

steps.title: Create an app
steps.text: Choose Scoped access, then Full Dropbox (App folder would limit the drive to a single folder; team folders need Full Dropbox). App names are global, so pick a unique one, not rclone. Click Create app.

steps.title: Grant the permissions
steps.text: On the Permissions tab tick account_info.read, files.metadata.write, files.content.write, files.content.read and sharing.write (the matching read boxes tick themselves), then click Submit.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI
steps.text: On the Settings tab, add this address under OAuth2 Redirect URIs.

steps.title: Copy the key and secret
steps.text: Also on the Settings tab: the App key is the client ID and the App secret (click Show) is the client secret.

id.label: App key
id.error: A Dropbox app key is a short code of letters and digits

secret.label: App secret
secret.error: A Dropbox app secret is a short code of letters and digits

onedrive.title: Your own OneDrive client
onedrive.why: rclone's built-in OneDrive client is shared by every rclone user and can get throttled. Registering your own is free; Azure asks you to create a free account first.

steps.title: Register an app
steps.text: In Microsoft Entra ID choose Add, then App registration. Any name. Supported accounts: any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts. Redirect URI: platform Web, with this address. Click Register.

steps.title: Copy the client ID
steps.text: On the app's Overview, copy the Application (client) ID.

steps.title: Create a client secret
steps.text: Certificates & secrets, New client secret, expiry 24 months. Copy its Value right away: it is shown only once (the Secret ID is not the secret).

steps.title: Grant the permissions
steps.text: API permissions, Add a permission, Microsoft Graph, Delegated permissions. Tick Files.Read, Files.ReadWrite, Files.Read.All, Files.ReadWrite.All, offline_access, User.Read and Sites.Read.All, then Add permissions.

onedrive.signin_note: Work and school accounts may need an administrator to approve the app. The secret expires after 24 months: set a new one here then.

secret.label: Client secret value
secret.error: That doesn't look like a secret value
secret.reject_error: That is the Secret ID. Copy the secret's Value instead

box.title: Your own Box app
box.why: Box limits API calls per app, and rclone's built-in app is shared by every rclone user. An app of your own is free.

steps.title: Create a custom app
steps.text: My Apps, Create New App, Custom App. Any name; for Purpose choose Automation. Click Next, choose User Authentication (OAuth 2.0), then Create App.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI
steps.text: On the Configuration tab, add this address under OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI.

steps.title: Set the scopes
steps.text: Under Application Scopes tick Read all files and folders stored in Box and Write all files and folders stored in Box. Leave the rest, then Save Changes.

steps.title: Copy the credentials
steps.text: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the same Configuration tab.

id.label: Client ID
id.error: A Box client ID is a long code of letters and digits

secret.label: Client secret
secret.error: A Box client secret is a long code of letters and digits

pcloud.title: Your own pCloud app
pcloud.why: rclone's built-in pCloud app is shared by every rclone user. An app of your own is free, and any pCloud account can own it.

steps.title: Create an app
steps.text: Sign in to pCloud's developer site with your pCloud account and create a new app with a unique name. Give it access to all folders, with write access.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI
steps.text: In the app's settings, add this address under Redirect URIs and save. Without it pCloud refuses the sign-in ("redirect_uri is not authorized").

steps.title: Copy the credentials
steps.text: The app's page shows its Client ID and Client secret.

pcloud.signin_note: US and EU accounts both work: the right pCloud server is found after you sign in.

id.label: Client ID
id.error: A pCloud client ID is a short code of letters and digits

secret.label: Client secret
secret.error: A pCloud client secret is a code of letters and digits
